chunks: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq (may God be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Hamadani, the client of Banu Hashim, narrated to us. He said: Al-Mundhir ibn Muhammad informed us. He said: Ja'far ibn Isma'il narrated to us from Abdullah ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, from al-Sadiq Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father (peace be upon them all), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: On the Day of Resurrection, a caller will call: 'Where is Zayn al-Abidin?' It is as though I am looking at my descendant Ali ibn al-Husayn ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib swaying between the rows.

key_terms.زين العابدين: Zayn al-Abidin — 'Ornament of the Worshipers', the epithet of the fourth Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS)
key_terms.مناد: A caller or herald; in eschatological contexts, an angel who makes announcements on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.يخطر: To walk with a swaying, majestic gait; implies nobility and dignified movement

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about Zayn al-Abidin on the Day of Resurrection?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) foretells a scene from the Day of Resurrection, where a heavenly caller announces Zayn al-Abidin — the title of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), meaning 'Ornament of the Worshipers.' The Prophet speaks as if witnessing the event himself, describing his descendant walking majestically between the rows of people on that day. This hadith was transmitted through a chain reaching back to Imam al-Husayn (AS) himself, adding particular poignancy given that the Prophet is speaking about a grandchild who would survive the tragedy of Karbala.
